title: 05. Advanced Python: 17. Magic (Dunder) Methods — Complete Catalog
summary: Dunder ("double underscore") methods let your classes integrate with Python's built-in protocols: arithmetic, iteration, context management, attribute access, and more.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: > Dunder ("double underscore") methods let your classes integrate with Python's built-in protocols: arithmetic, iteration, context management, attribute access, and more.

sections.title: 1. The Big Picture
sections.body:
| Category                 | Purpose                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Construction & lifecycle | `__new__`, `__init__`, `__del__`                                                                                  |
| String representations   | `__repr__`, `__str__`, `__format__`, `__bytes__`                                                                  |
| Comparison & hashing     | `__eq__`, `__lt__`, `__le__`, `__gt__`, `__ge__`, `__ne__`, `__hash__`                                            |
| Numeric / arithmetic     | `__add__`, `__sub__`, …, `__radd__`, `__iadd__`, …                                                                |
| Unary & conversion       | `__neg__`, `__abs__`, `__int__`, `__float__`, `__bool__`, `__index__`, `__round__`                                |
| Container protocol       | `__len__`, `__getitem__`, `__setitem__`, `__delitem__`, `__contains__`, `__iter__`, `__reversed__`, `__missing__` |
| Callable                 | `__call__`                                                                                                        |
| Attribute access         | `__getattr__`, `__getattribute__`, `__setattr__`, `__delattr__`, `__dir__`                                        |
| Context manager          | `__enter__`, `__exit__`, `__aenter__`, `__aexit__`                                                                |
| Descriptor               | `__get__`, `__set__`, `__delete__`, `__set_name__`                                                                |
| Class hooks              | `__init_subclass__`, `__class_getitem__`, `__mro_entries__`, `__instancecheck__`, `__subclasscheck__`             |
| Pickling / copy          | `__reduce__`, `__reduce_ex__`, `__getstate__`, `__setstate__`, `__copy__`, `__deepcopy__`                         |
| Async iteration          | `__aiter__`, `__anext__`                                                                                          |
| Misc                     | `__slots__`, `__dict__`, `__class__`, `__doc__`, `__module__`                                                     |

sections.title: 2. Construction & Lifecycle
sections.body:
```python
class Singleton:
    _inst = None
    def __new__(cls, *a, **kw):           # creates the instance
        if cls._inst is None:
            cls._inst = super().__new__(cls)
        return cls._inst

    def __init__(self, value):            # initializes the instance
        self.value = value
```

- `__new__` is a **static method** that returns the new instance.
- `__init__` runs only if `__new__` returns an instance of `cls`.
- `__del__` is called when refcount hits zero. **Avoid** for cleanup — use context managers. Cycles + `__del__` were a problem pre-3.4 (now fine, but still discouraged).

sections.title: 3. Representation
4. Comparison & Hashing
5. Arithmetic & Reflected / In-place
sections.body:
For each binary op there are three variants:

| Op        | Method                    | Reflected                    | In-place        |
| --------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- | -------- |
| `+`       | `__add__`                 | `__radd__`                   | `__iadd__`      |
| `-`       | `__sub__`                 | `__rsub__`                   | `__isub__`      |
| `*`       | `__mul__`                 | `__rmul__`                   | `__imul__`      |
| `/`       | `__truediv__`             | `__rtruediv__`               | `__itruediv__`  |
| `//`      | `__floordiv__`            | `__rfloordiv__`              | `__ifloordiv__` |
| `%`       | `__mod__`                 | `__rmod__`                   | `__imod__`      |
| `**`      | `__pow__`                 | `__rpow__`                   | `__ipow__`      |
| `<<` `>>` | `__lshift__` `__rshift__` | `__r…__`                     | `__i…__`        |
| `&` `     | ` `^`                     | `__and__` `__or__` `__xor__` | `__r…__`        | `__i…__` |
| `@`       | `__matmul__`              | `__rmatmul__`                | `__imatmul__`   |

```python
class Vec:
    def __init__(self, x, y): self.x, self.y = x, y
    def __add__(self, o):  return Vec(self.x+o.x, self.y+o.y)
    def __mul__(self, k):  return Vec(self.x*k, self.y*k)   # vec * scalar
    def __rmul__(self, k): return self.__mul__(k)            # scalar * vec
    def __iadd__(self, o):                                   # in-place +=
        self.x += o.x; self.y += o.y; return self
```

**Reflected** is called when the left operand doesn't support the op (or returns `NotImplemented`). E.g., `2 * vec` calls `vec.__rmul__(2)`.

**In-place** is what `+=` looks for; if missing, falls back to `__add__` and rebinds the name (which is why `tuple += ...` works but doesn't mutate).

sections.title: 6. Unary & Conversion
sections.body:
```python
__neg__, __pos__, __abs__, __invert__   # -x, +x, abs(x), ~x

__int__       # int(obj)
__float__     # float(obj)
__complex__   # complex(obj)
__bool__      # bool(obj); fallback to __len__ != 0 if absent; default True
__index__     # __int__ used by int(), but __index__ used by slicing/bin()/oct()/hex()
__round__     # round(obj, ndigits)
__trunc__, __floor__, __ceil__         # math.*
```

`__index__` is what enables your object to be used as a list index — implement it for integer-like custom types.

sections.title: 7. Container Protocol
8. Callable — __call__
sections.body:
Make instances behave like functions:

```python
class Multiplier:
    def __init__(self, k): self.k = k
    def __call__(self, x): return self.k * x

mul3 = Multiplier(3)
mul3(10)        # 30
```

Class-based decorators rely on this.

sections.title: 9. Attribute Access
10. Context Managers
sections.body:
```python
class Resource:
    def __enter__(self): self.h = open_resource(); return self.h
    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
        close_resource(self.h)
        return False    # don't suppress exceptions
```

Async variant:

```python
class AsyncResource:
    async def __aenter__(self): ...
    async def __aexit__(self, et, e, tb): ...
```

(See chapter 06 for full deep dive.)

sections.title: 11. Descriptors
12. Class Creation Hooks
13. Pickling
sections.body:
```python
class State:
    def __init__(self, conn, cache):
        self.conn = conn        # not picklable
        self.cache = cache

    def __getstate__(self):
        d = self.__dict__.copy()
        d.pop("conn", None)     # exclude unpicklable
        return d

    def __setstate__(self, state):
        self.__dict__.update(state)
        self.conn = reconnect()
```

`__reduce__` is the lowest level — return a tuple Python uses to reconstruct the object. Used for very custom serialization.

sections.title: 14. Copying
sections.body:
```python
import copy
class Big:
    def __copy__(self):     return Big(...)            # shallow
    def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
        new = Big(...)
        memo[id(self)] = new                            # avoid infinite recursion
        new.children = copy.deepcopy(self.children, memo)
        return new
```

sections.title: 15. Async Iteration
sections.body:
```python
class AsyncCounter:
    def __init__(self, n): self.n = n
    def __aiter__(self): self.i = 0; return self
    async def __anext__(self):
        if self.i >= self.n: raise StopAsyncIteration
        self.i += 1; return self.i

async def main():
    async for x in AsyncCounter(3):
        print(x)
```

sections.title: 16. Style Guidelines
sections.body:
| Do                                                          | Don't                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Use `NotImplemented` for unsupported types in operators     | raise `TypeError` directly             |
| Make `__repr__` unambiguous and ideally evaluable           | dump opaque object addresses           |
| Set `__hash__ = None` for mutable types overriding `__eq__` | leave hash inherited                   |
| Use `super().__setattr__` to avoid recursion                | call `self.x = …` inside `__setattr__` |
| Use `__set_name__` for descriptors                          | hardcode attribute names               |
| Use context managers instead of `__del__` for cleanup       | rely on GC timing                      |
